text:
Bobby Brink grew up in Minnetonka, and since coming to the Wild from Philadelphia he has played like someone happy to be home, and sometimes like someone who cares a little too much. Last week in Toronto he smashed his stick after missing on a 3-on-1, a clip that made the rounds. Days later in a rout of Boston he ended up in a fight with Charlie McAvoy, who, per a Markerzone headline, faces a possible suspension after the fight.

The Duluth News Tribune says he found another level on the road trip, and the Athletic's Michael Russo wrote about his second wind. The numbers mostly agree. Minnesota takes 56% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, four points better than without him. He has 11 points in 23 games, but only two goals on 4.8 expected; he's shooting 5.4% when the league sits at 13.4.

That stick-smash makes sense, then. The chances are there and the finish isn't. Goals tend to follow looks like these, and a player driving play on a third line is more valuable than his goal total says.
headline: Brink is making noise in his home state
